title: Domaine des Cyprès
area: Heart of the peninsula, private gated estate
features: Belle Époque guest house with six bedrooms
Walk to the beach and the village
short: Two houses among cypress and pine at the centre of Cap Ferrat, a short walk from the sea.
long: A private estate of some five and a half thousand square metres, held within a gated domain at the heart of the peninsula. The main house opens onto long terraces and an infinity pool, with a cellar, a lift to every level and a quiet wellness area. Across the garden stands a Belle Époque guest house of six bedrooms, entirely its own. Cypress and Mediterranean planting frame every view. The village, the harbour and a sandy beach are all within an easy walk.

title: Maison Édouard
area: Avenue Édouard VII, on the heights
short: A restored Belle Époque villa above Beaulieu, with an infinity pool and the whole bay below.
long: Built around 1900 on the avenue Édouard VII, this villa sits above the town with the sea laid out in front of it. A careful restoration has kept the proportions and the light while making the house quiet and easy to live in. Three floors face south, joined by a lift, with four suites, a glass winter garden and a lawn that runs to the edge of an infinity pool. The harbour, the market and the cafés of Beaulieu are a few minutes on foot.

title: Bastide de la Rade
area: Above the old town, facing the bay
features: Panoramic views over the bay and Cap Ferrat
short: A stone bastide with a tower, looking straight across the bay of Villefranche to Cap Ferrat.
long: Pale stone, a round tower and terraces of old terracotta, set just above the town yet entirely private. Every principal room turns toward the bay of Villefranche and the green line of Cap Ferrat beyond. Inside, the ceilings are high and the mouldings original, with five bedrooms en suite. Gardens of cypress and bougainvillea step down to a pool with the same view. A staff apartment, a lift and a garage for three cars complete the house.

title: Villa Cap Fleuri
type: Waterfront Belle Époque villa to restore
features: Pool and garden on the shore
short: A white villa of 1900 on the rocks at Cap Fleuri, the sea at the foot of the garden.
long: Rarely does a house sit this close to the water. Built around 1900 in the Cap Fleuri quarter, the main villa keeps its white columns, broad stone steps and tall shuttered windows, with a garden and pool that end at the rocks. A second house stands apart for family or staff. Both now ask for a complete restoration, which leaves the next owner free to shape the interiors entirely. Monaco is a few minutes along the coast.

title: Le Belvédère
area: Cap de Nice, Palais Maeterlinck, below Mont Boron
features: 171 m² wooden terrace over the sea
short: A duplex above the open sea at Cap de Nice, with its own pool and a funicular to the shore.
long: Within the Palais Maeterlinck on Cap de Nice, between Mont Boron and the Baie des Anges, this duplex of close to five hundred square metres faces nothing but water. The upper floor is given to one long room of light, opening onto a wooden terrace with a private pool and an outdoor kitchen. Below are the principal suite and three further bedrooms. A private funicular descends to the residence beach. A studio and a double garage complete it.

title: Les Pins
short: A new house of stone, glass and pale oak among umbrella pines above Èze Bord de Mer.
long: Completed in 2025, this house sits among old umbrella pines above the water at Èze Bord de Mer, between Monaco and Cap Ferrat. Pale stone floors, oak and tall glass keep the rooms quiet and full of light. The living spaces open level onto a garden, rare on this steep coast, and a fourteen metre infinity pool. Upstairs, a principal suite of more than sixty square metres and two further bedrooms share a terrace facing the sea.

title: Bastide des Prés
area: Countryside near Grasse, Valbonne and Opio
features: Nearly 3 hectares of meadow in a protected zone
Pool among restored stone lime kilns
short: A stone farmhouse of 1850 in three hectares of meadow and plane trees, near Grasse.
long: A nineteenth century farmhouse of honey coloured stone, standing in almost three hectares of open meadow in a protected natural area outside Châteauneuf. Plane trees shade the terrace, a long pond holds the reflection of the house, and the pool lies among restored stone kilns of the same age. Inside, linen, light and a fireplace; eight bedrooms in all, with a winter garden and a separate guest house. Cannes, Antibes and Nice airport are within twenty five minutes.
